_comment: ticket #470 — the ONE declaration of the glibc root filesystem this terminal ships inside its APK and enters through proot, so a fresh install is ready for agent coding with no network and no first-run installs. It does NOT carry a copy of the fleet tool belt: `shared_toolbelt` points at cloud-u-containers/_shared/agent-toolbelt.json (#509) by commit sha, and every apt package, tarball and verified binary declared there is installed here too. The keys below are ONLY what a phone terminal needs on top of what every AI container already gets, and the tester fails if any of them repeats a shared entry, so this can never grow into a second copy of that list. Read by rootfs/build-rootfs.sh (CI builds the tree), rootfs/verify-rootfs.sh (CI proves it runs under the proot that ships) and app/build.gradle (asset directory name).

shared_toolbelt._doc: Why a pinned fetch and not a copy: the two repositories are separate git histories, so a file cannot be shared by path. Both are public, so CI reads the file at this exact commit from raw.githubusercontent.com. The commit sha is the content address: bumping it is an edit to THIS file, which moves the publish gate's source identity, so a tool-belt change republishes the APK instead of hiding outside the gate. Bump `ref` to the latest commit that touched `path` when the fleet list changes.

base_image._doc: Multi-architecture index digest of debian:bookworm-slim, so arm64 and amd64 builds start from the same pinned snapshot. glibc is the whole point: claude, node and antigravity publish linux-gnu builds, which Android's bionic cannot load (#288). proot supplies this root so their PT_INTERP resolves.

_doc_apt_packages: Terminal-only additions, installed together with the shared apt_packages. git: the shared list counts it as a base-image binary of the AI containers, and debian slim does not carry it. fish: the default shell. zsh: baked and available, NOT the default (#470 follow-up). python3-venv: hermes is installed into its own virtual environment (pip_venvs below). python3: already pulled in by python3-venv, named so the roster can declare it (#737; this terminal's extra, not the shared toolset -- #665 keeps it out of the nix image). age: bookworm ships 1.1.1, the shared toolset's encryption tool. debianutils: provides `which`, which the toolset declares because the on-device checklist runs it. util-linux and diffutils: flock and cmp, which the toolset declares because linux-store (store.json::linux_tools) refuses to start without them; both are Essential in bookworm, named so the roster can declare them.
_doc_apt_provides: Same meaning as the fleet tool belt's apt_provides (package -> binary names when they differ), for packages only this terminal installs. resolve.py merges both maps.

node._doc: Node 22 LTS from nodejs.org rather than Debian's nodejs 18 + ~300 node-* packages. Carries npm and npx, which claude's MCP servers are launched with.

goose._doc: Same release the fleet's my-ai-api image installs (user-ai_my-ai-api/src/code/Dockerfile, GOOSE_VER). The -unknown-linux-gnu build: glibc, which is why it needs this root and cannot run against bionic.

agy._doc: Google Antigravity's agent CLI (google-antigravity/antigravity-cli), the component the termux flake already ships as `agy`. NOT the Antigravity IDE: that is an Electron GUI (apt repo us-central1-apt.pkg.dev/projects/antigravity-auto-updater-dev, arm64 1.23.2 exists, 725 MB unpacked plus GTK/X11) and a terminal with no X server cannot display it — #470's first brief said to ship the CLI when one exists. The archive holds one glibc ELF named `antigravity` (PT_INTERP /lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 on arm64, measured), installed as /usr/local/bin/agy.

fd._doc: #737 -- fd for the shared toolset. Debian packages it as fd-find with the binary renamed to fdfind, so the upstream release is used instead; the musl build is static, so it needs nothing from this root.

sops._doc: #737 -- sops for the shared toolset; not packaged in bookworm. The release asset IS the binary (a static Go build).

npm_globals._doc: Installed with the node above. claude-code publishes a native binary per platform as optionalDependencies; npm picks the linux-gnu one for this glibc root.

pip_venvs._doc: Python agents, each in its own venv so their pins cannot fight Debian's python3 packages. hermes-agent is Nous Research's PyPI release of the agent the fleet runs as the hermes-agent container (that image is built FROM nousresearch/hermes-agent, which installs this same project); its pyproject declares the `hermes` console script. requires-python >=3.11,<3.14 — bookworm's python3 is 3.11.

_doc_binaries: This terminal's tools BEYOND ab_cloud-terminal-store/store.json::toolset (#737: fish, zsh, node, claude, gh, ... -- the set both terminals ship) and beyond the fleet tool belt's `binaries`. resolve.py merges all three into the roster install-in-rootfs.sh installs and command -v's and verify-rootfs.sh proves present, loadable (PT_INTERP inside the root) and executable under the shipped proot. A name repeated from either other list is refused.
_doc_default_shell: Written into the rootfs as root's login shell (/etc/passwd). The device entry script (rootfs/enter.sh) does not name a shell: it reads root's entry from the extracted rootfs, so this key is the only place the default lives.

smoke._doc: Commands that must print something under proot. Each command's first word must be a declared binary.

_doc_nameservers: docker export leaves /etc/resolv.conf empty, and Android has no /etc/resolv.conf to bind in, so build-rootfs.sh writes one from this list. #741: it names NO public server any more (it named two public resolvers, Cloudflare's and Google's, so every shell lookup went past the SuperApp's DNS menu and past Private DNS). 127.0.0.1 is the bridge: enter.sh runs proot with -p, which moves a guest's :53 on loopback to dns_bridge.port, where the app answers every query with Android's own resolver (libs/sysdns SystemDnsBridge). glibc, musl, Go and node in this tree all reach it the same way; rootfs/verify-rootfs.sh resolves a name through it under the shipped proot and goes red without -p.

dns_bridge._doc: Where the bridge listens is libs:sysdns's to declare (bridge_port), not this file's: the app that answers and the tester that proves the path both read it there.

proot._doc: #795 The proot this terminal ships is ab_cloud-terminal-store/proot.json's, the one the nix terminal ships too (build-rootfs.sh stages it with fetch-proot.py). Static means no PT_INTERP: the same binary runs on bionic Android and on the glibc CI runner, so CI tests the exact bytes the phone executes. The two keys below name the copy it replaced, the bootstrap-release-24.05 one #348 pinned in the nix app's build.json: verify-rootfs.sh runs it as the mutant the pty selftest must fail under, so the selftest is proven to see the phone's 2026-10-03 failure.

_doc_asset_dir: APK assets/<asset_dir>/ holds rootfs.sha256, rootfs.url, proot and enter.sh — four small files, NOT the tree. #618: the tree is fetched once from the artifact declared below, verified against rootfs.sha256 and cached. The app stages the small files under $PREFIX/var/lib/<asset_dir>/, fetches the tarball next to them, and enter.sh extracts it there on first shell.

artifact._doc: #618 — the rootfs tarball is a SEPARATELY VERSIONED release asset, not APK bytes. It is ~400 MB and it changes only when the declaration below changes, while the APK's code changes constantly; baked in, every one-line app fix made every phone re-download 400 MB. Published to the app's own rolling GH release (the same channel and the same repo as the APK, so no new infrastructure and no new host), fetched on first run and whenever the declared digest moves, and never again.
artifact._doc_id: {id} is the first 12 hex of sha256 over identity_files, so the asset name IS the content address of the declaration that produces the tree. A pin bump (claude-code, node, the tool-belt ref, the build script) yields a NEW name: it is uploaded, its digest is baked into the next APK, and every phone refetches. An app-code change yields the SAME name: nothing is uploaded and no phone refetches. That is why there is no hand-maintained version number to forget to bump. {abi} is the release.variants[] id.
artifact._doc_identity_files_linux_tools: store.json::linux_tools: build-rootfs.sh installs the pinned linux-store, linux-account and fish greeting into the tree through fetch-linux-tools.py, so the fetcher's bytes (and, through store.json, the pin and the hashes) address the tarball.
artifact._doc_identity_files_771: #771 -- build-rootfs.sh compiles noexec-shebang.c into the tree (/usr/local/lib, listed in /etc/ld.so.preload) and installs gitconfig as /etc/gitconfig: both are bytes of the tarball, so both address it.
artifact._doc_identity_files_toolset: #737 -- store.json carries the shared toolset, which decides what this tree installs. Left out, a toolset edit would keep the old asset name: nothing uploads, no phone refetches, CI green over a rootfs without the new tool. Relative to the app dir, like every entry here.
artifact._doc_assets: The two small files baked into the APK in the tarball's place: the sha256 the fetch is gated on, and the resolved url it is fetched from. Both are written by the publish step from THIS declaration, so the phone never carries a hardcoded url.

_doc_abis: Keyed by the Android ABI from build.json release.variants[].abis. The rootfs is built and tested on a runner of the SAME CPU, natively: no qemu, so what the tester executes is what the phone executes.
